en: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, he said: I heard Abu Ishaq say: I heard al-Bara' saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was a man of medium height, broad between the shoulders, with hair flowing down to the lobes of his ears. He was wearing a red suit; I have never seen anything more handsome than him (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).
Abu al-Tahir narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, with this chain of transmission, similar to it.

Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim and Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Ziyad narrated to us—Mansur said: narrated to us, and Ibn Ja'far said: Ibrahim informed us, meaning Ibn Sa'd—from Ibn Shihab, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah, from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: The People of the Book used to let their hair hang down freely, while the polytheists used to part their hair, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) liked to conform with the People of the Book in what he had not been commanded regarding. So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) let his forelock hang down, then he parted it afterwards.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Hitan ibn 'Abdullah al-Raqashi, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, he said: When revelation descended upon the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), he would lower his head, and his Companions would lower their heads; then when it ceased, he would raise his head.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Hitan ibn 'Abdullah, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, he said: When revelation descended upon the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), he felt distressed by it and his face turned ashen.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us; (H) and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Usamah and Ibn Bishr narrated to us, all from Hisham; (H) and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us—and the wording is his—Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from 'A'ishah, that al-Harith ibn Hisham asked the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "How does revelation come to you?" He said: "Sometimes it comes to me like the ringing of a bell, and that is the hardest upon me; then it departs from me while I have comprehended it. And sometimes an angel comes in the form of a man, and I comprehend what he says."

Abu Kurayb, Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from 'A'ishah, she said: Revelation would descend upon the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) on a bitterly cold morning, and yet his forehead would stream with sweat.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, from Umm Sulaym, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to visit her and take a midday nap at her place, so she would spread a leather mat for him and he would take a midday nap on it. He used to perspire profusely, so she would collect his sweat and put it in perfume and glass bottles. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "O Umm Sulaym, what is this?" She said: "Your sweat; I mix it with my perfume."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me, Hujayn ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz—who is Ibn Abi Salamah—narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik, he said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to enter the house of Umm Sulaym and sleep on her bed when she was not there. He said: One day he came and slept on her bed. She was approached and it was said to her: "Here is the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) asleep in your house on your bed." He said: So she came while he was sweating, and his sweat had pooled on a piece of leather on the bed. She opened her scent box and began wiping up that sweat and squeezing it into her bottles. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) woke up startled and said: "What are you doing, O Umm Sulaym?" She said: "O Messenger of Allah, we hope for its blessing for our children." He said: "You have done right."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Hashim—meaning Ibn al-Qasim—narrated to us, from Sulayman, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, he said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) visited us and took a midday nap at our house, and he perspired. My mother came with a bottle and began scraping the sweat into it. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) awoke and said: "O Umm Sulaym, what is this you are doing?" She said: "This is your sweat; we add it to our perfume, and it is the finest of perfume."

Ahmad ibn Sa'id ibn Sakhr al-Darimi narrated to me, Habban narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, from Anas, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had a luminous complexion; his sweat was like pearls; when he walked, he leaned forward. And I never touched brocade or silk softer than the palm of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), nor did I ever smell musk or ambergris more fragrant than the scent of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas; (H) and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me—and the wording is his—Hashim—meaning Ibn al-Qasim—narrated to us, Sulayman—who is Ibn al-Mughirah—narrated to us, from Thabit: Anas said: I never smelled ambergris, nor musk, nor anything more fragrant than the fragrance of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). And I never touched anything of brocade or silk softer to the touch than the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).

'Amr ibn Hammad ibn Talhah al-Qannad narrated to us, Asbat—who is Ibn Nasr al-Hamdani—narrated to us, from Simak, from Jabir ibn Samurah, he said: I prayed the first prayer (Zuhr) with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), then he went out to his family and I went out with him. Some children met him, and he began gently wiping the cheeks of each of them, one by one. He said: As for me, he wiped my cheek, and I felt for his hand a coolness and fragrance as if he had brought it out from a perfumer's chest.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, they said: 'Abdah and Waki' narrated to us; (H) and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, all of them from Hisham, with this chain of transmission, some of them adding to the others.

Abu Kurayb narrated it to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from 'A'ishah, she said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) never struck anything with his hand—neither a woman nor a servant—except when fighting in the cause of Allah. Nor was he ever wronged in anything so as to take revenge upon its perpetrator, unless something from the sanctities of Allah was violated, in which case he would take revenge for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

And Abu Kurayb and Ibn Numayr both narrated it to us from 'Abdullah ibn Numayr, from Hisham, with this chain of transmission up to his words: "the easier of the two." And they did not mention what followed it.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from 'A'ishah, she said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was never given the choice between two matters, one being easier than the other, except that he chose the easier of them, as long as it was not a sin. But if it was a sin, he was the furthest of people from it.
And Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated it to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, with this chain of transmission, similar to the hadith of Malik.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, both from Jarir; (H) and Ahmad ibn 'Abdah narrated to us, Fudayl ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, both from Mansur, from Muhammad—in the narration of Fudayl: Ibn Shihab, and in the narration of Jarir: Muhammad al-Zuhri—from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Malik ibn Anas in what was recited to him; (H) and Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from 'A'ishah, wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that she said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was never given the choice between two matters except that he took the easier of them, as long as it was not a sin. But if it was a sin, he was the furthest of people from it. Nor did the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) ever take revenge for himself, unless a sanctity of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was violated.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Anas, that a woman had some mental deficiency, so she said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have a need from you." He said: "O mother of so-and-so, see whichever side-street you wish, so that I may fulfill your need for you." So he stood alone with her in one of the pathways until she finished presenting her need.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us, Abu al-Nadr narrated to us, Sulayman narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) while the barber was shaving him, and his Companions were encircling him, desiring that not a single hair should fall except into the hand of a man.

Mujahid ibn Musa, Abu Bakr ibn al-Nadr ibn Abi al-Nadr, and Harun ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us, all from Abu al-Nadr; Abu Bakr said: Abu al-Nadr—meaning Hashim ibn al-Qasim—narrated to us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, he said: When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had prayed the morning prayer (Fajr), the servants of Medina would bring their vessels containing water, and no vessel was brought to him except that he dipped his hand in it. Sometimes they would bring them to him on a cold morning, and he would still dip his hand in it.

And Ibn Bashshar narrated it to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he did not mention: "a camel-driver with a beautiful voice."

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Hammam narrated to me, Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had a camel-driver with a beautiful voice, so the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: "Slowly, O Anjashah! Do not break the glass vessels"—meaning the delicate women.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Yazid ibn Zuray' informed us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Anas ibn Malik; (H) and Abu Kamil narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, al-Taymi narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, he said: Umm Sulaym was with the wives of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and a camel-driver was driving them fast. The Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "O Anjashah, go gently in driving the glass vessels!"

'Amr al-Naqid and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, both from Ibn 'Ulayyah; Zuhayr said: Isma'il narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came upon his wives while a camel-driver called Anjashah was driving their camels fast, so he said: "Woe to you, O Anjashah! Go gently in driving the glass vessels." He said: Abu Qilabah said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) spoke a word which, had one of you uttered it, you would have criticized him for it.
Abu al-Rabi' al-'Ataki, Hamid ibn 'Umar, and Abu Kamil narrated to us, they said: Hammad narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, similar to it.

Abu al-Rabi' al-'Ataki, Hamid ibn 'Umar, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, and Abu Kamil narrated to us, all from Hammad ibn Zayd; Abu al-Rabi' said: Hammad narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was on one of his journeys, and a black boy named Anjashah was singing camel songs to urge them on. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: "O Anjashah, go gently in driving the glass vessels!"

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu Khaythamah informed us, from Simak ibn Harb, he said: I said to Jabir ibn Samurah: "Did you use to sit with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)?" He said: "Yes, frequently. He would not stand up from his prayer-place where he prayed the morning prayer (Fajr) until the sun rose; when it rose, he would stand up. And they would converse, discussing affairs of the pre-Islamic period of ignorance and laughing, while he (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) would smile."
